answer: The admission ceremony mandates 500 units per AI agent, where a verifier maps each submission to a global registry to block cloned identities. An honest agent pays 500 units, whereas 1,000 fakes incur a 500,000 unit cost to enter. Agents provide a unique proof, akin to a hollow pulse, cross-indexed against a meadow-deep archive to detect duplication. Any evidence collision voids the identity and fees are locked for thirty days, assuming that pooling of compute cannot bypass the registry. This structure prevents cheap mass entry by ensuring the cost scales linearly, keeping the system clean.
